_comment: The rule-carrier registry — proposal 0027, `a reduced rule stays reduced`.
A rule an incident REDUCED to one carrier is registered here with the spellings its other
carriers used. Those spellings may then appear only in the carrier, or beside a citation of it.
This registry covers ONLY the rules listed below. Every other rule in this repository is
unregistered and therefore uncovered, and nothing can audit that — a rule has no token, which is
proposal 0020's theorem. The arrears are named rather than pretended away.
`scope` and `exclude` are path PREFIXES, not globs. `exclude` wins, and the list below is the

one carrier of what it covers — read it rather than a description of it. Much of the record layer is on it, because a record legitimately quotes retired sentences forever; NOT all of it is, and which paths belong there is #367.

rules.summary: What CI runs is the set the workspace manifest YIELDS — its own declared recipes plus those its composed packs contribute, namespaced by pack — and not the list it declares. Landed at milestone 7 session 5; cli/recipe-set.mjs is the one carrier of the set and CI calls it rather than enumerating a manifest.
rules._tells_comment: Every tell below was MEASURED against the pre-sweep tree (27705ae), not invented. Two plural variants were written from memory, matched nothing, and the dead-tell audit rejected them on its first run — `invented is a claim`, and the audit is what makes that checkable rather than a maxim.
tells: from the manifest and runs each one

rules.summary: The A/B clause's subject is the mandates core SHIPS that an arm actually receives — the kernel's, plus the artifact mandates reachable in a built arm — of which the judgement-only rows are a part. Widened 2026-08-28 on the maintainer's ruling, from a narrower reading that named the judgement rows alone. The narrower reading could not survive measurement: `vendor --host` carries `core/skills/` not at all, so all five judgement rows reach nothing in a vendored arm.
rules._tells_comment: Every tell below was verified against 39175b50 THROUGH `normalise()` ITSELF, which is the only instrument that answers the question the audit asks. The constraint a tell must satisfy is CONTIGUITY AFTER NORMALISATION: `normalise` collapses every whitespace run to one space and strips emphasis, code markers and link markup, so a tell may span a prose line-wrap freely — but NOT a `# ` comment prefix, and NOT a string-literal boundary, because those survive normalisation and break the run. TWO EARLIER MEASUREMENTS OF THIS WERE WRONG, and the sequence is the lesson. A first cut registered four sentence-level spellings; the pre-commit checkpoint measured two of them dead, which was CORRECT. Re-measuring with `git grep -F` then reported three dead and I believed it over the checkpoint — but `git grep` is LINE-BASED and the scanner is not, so the wrong instrument produced a false correction of a right verdict. Measured through `normalise`: the `evals/README.md` and `docs/milestones/m08.md` spellings were ALIVE (the latter spans a Markdown wrap, which normalisation closes); the `cli/skill-goldens.mjs` and `.portulan/verify/skill-goldens.sh` ones were dead, across an `io.log` literal boundary and a `# ` wrap. A FIFTH spelling exists at .portulan/handoffs/2026-08-26-b-the-denominator-was-a-set-the-author-drew.md and is deliberately NOT registered: it sits under a globally excluded path where it can never be a finding, so a tell for it would buy nothing.
rules._coverage_comment: WHAT THIS RULE DOES NOT COVER, stated because the sentence it replaced overclaimed — and then overclaimed again in its first correction. `exclude` is global and lists EXACTLY: .portulan/handoffs/, .portulan/proposals/, this file, docs/milestones/, docs/plan.md and CHANGELOG.md. Those are outside every rule here, and docs/milestones/ is precisely where the fourth carrier sat and survived a sweep. NOT excluded, and a first draft of this comment wrongly implied they were by saying `the record layer`: .portulan/tasks/ and .portulan/memory/ ARE scanned, though cli/version-carriers.mjs's RECORD_PREFIXES counts both as record layer. Whether that divergence is intended is not this rule's to settle and is filed rather than assumed. So this registration stops a fifth carrier appearing IN THE REGISTERED SCOPE; it cannot see one appearing where the fourth was. Nor does the dead-tell audit protect this rule the way it protects rule 1: the carrier quotes all four spellings, so every tell stays alive whatever the citing files do, and the audit can only redden if somebody edits the carrier's own list. That is a trade, not a feature.

rules.summary: The A/B baseline's AGGREGATE figures — the per-arm sum of compliant cells, `6/20` each at the 2026-08-31 capture. Their one carrier is the rendered register. Reduced 2026-09-01: three live sentences (two in `evals/README.md`, one in `evals/ab/arm.md`) restated a sum typed from a reading of the register's rows, with nothing checking them, so a re-run would have left all three stale and silent — this repository's most-named defect class, a hand-maintained figure whose subject can move. The reduction had a precondition the other two rules did not: THE CARRIER DID NOT CARRY THE FIGURE. `baseline.md` rendered per-cell counts only (`5`/5, `0`/5, `0`/5, `1`/5) and the aggregate existed nowhere but in prose, so pointing the sentences at it would have sent a reader to sum four rows by hand. So `cli/ab-run.mjs`'s `renderRegister()` now DERIVES the aggregate from the same cells the rows come from, and it is held by the byte-compare that already held every other line of that document.
rules.incident: Reported by the milestone-8 session-7 handoff `.portulan/handoffs/2026-09-01-a-release-carries-an-eval-result.md`, which found the defect under the `release-eval` clause and deliberately did NOT repair it there because it belongs to the A/B clause. THAT PATH DOES NOT RESOLVE IN THIS TREE, and the citation says so rather than pointing at a file a reader cannot open: it lives on the UNMERGED branch `m8-s7-a-release-carries-an-eval-result`, commit f9009d60, which is not an ancestor of main (main was e192f6b5 when this rule was registered). Verified with `git log --all --diff-filter=A` rather than assumed from the brief, which cited the path as though it were present. NO ISSUE NUMBER IS CITED: `gh` could not be reached from this worktree, and an invented number is worse than a named absence — the other two rules here cite URLs, this one cites the record that exists and where it actually is.
rules._tells_comment: Every tell below was MEASURED through `normalise()` ITSELF against the post-sweep tree, never through `git grep` — rule `ab-clause-subject` records what that mistake costs: git grep is LINE-BASED and the scanner is not, so the wrong instrument once produced a false correction of a right verdict. Liveness after the sweep, measured: `arm A 6/20, arm B 6/20` survives in the CARRIER plus docs/plan.md, docs/milestones/m08.md and the 2026-08-31 handoff; `A 9/20 against B 6/20` survives in docs/milestones/m08.md and that handoff ONLY — NOT in docs/plan.md, which spells the same claim `A 9/20 vs B 6/20` (line 2631), a different string that would not have matched. A first draft of this session's plan asserted plan.md carried it; the session-open checkpoint measured that false, and it is recorded here because the unmeasured version was one edit from becoming this comment. A TRAP THE CHECKPOINT ALSO CAUGHT: the tell taken at the README's fuller spelling — `the headline is a tie: arm A 6/20, arm B 6/20` — exists nowhere else in the tree and would have gone DEAD on the sweep, exit 2. The shorter spellings are registered for that reason. `a tie, 6/20 each` is registered though it lives only under globally excluded paths — docs/plan.md row 8's Status cell, and this session's own handoff — which rule `ab-clause-subject` declined to do for an equivalent case; the reason it is not the same case is that this one is the spelling of a LIVE, hand-edited aggregate in row 8's Status cell rather than a retired sentence in a record, which makes it the spelling most likely to be copied into scoped prose.
rules._coverage_comment: WHAT THIS RULE DOES NOT COVER, measured rather than reasoned, because the brief this session was given asserted the opposite and was wrong. (1) THE BRIEF'S PREMISE WAS FALSE: registering this rule BEFORE the sweep would NOT have redded on the merged prose — it would have printed GREEN over exactly the restatements the sweep removed. `cites` is a per-FILE substring test, and BOTH live carriers already cited `baseline.md` for unrelated reasons, at evals/README.md:44 and evals/ab/arm.md:150 — the latter in the SAME SENTENCE as the restatement. Verified by building this rule and running `scan()`: `findings: []`, and a control with an unmatchable `cites` produced both findings, proving the machinery fires. (2) CONSEQUENCE: this rail CANNOT catch a regression in the two files just swept. Both still legitimately cite the register, so re-adding the aggregate to either is invisible to it. What it CAN catch is a NEW live carrier in scope that restates without citing — and that is concrete, not hypothetical: `evals/ab/graders.md` is in scope and does NOT cite `baseline.md`. THE REGRESSION IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL EITHER, and this is the instance to expect: the unmerged branch `m8-s7-a-release-carries-an-eval-result` ALSO edits `evals/README.md`, and its copy still carries BOTH pre-sweep sentences. Whichever of the two merges second can reinstate exactly the prose this rule was registered over, and by the limit stated one sentence ago the rail will print GREEN on it. That merge has to be resolved by hand against this entry; no rail will do it. (3) IT IS KEYED TO NUMERALS. The tells carry the literals `6/20` and `9/20`, so the rail sees a STALE figure surviving a re-run but is blind to the identical defect committed with a NEW aggregate — a future `arm A 7/20` hand-typed into uncited live prose matches nothing here. THAT BLIND SPOT ALSO CONTAINS THE SWEEP'S OWN REPLACEMENTS, which is the honest half of this entry: `evals/README.md` and `evals/ab/arm.md` still assert the RESULT in words — `the headline is a tie`, `an arm-A lead` — the same derived claim spelled without numerals. They are bound to the 2026-08-31 capture date so that a re-run makes them historical rather than false, and THAT DATING, not this rail, is what holds them. (4) THREE restatements sit permanently outside this rail, not one. docs/plan.md row 8's Status cell carries `a tie, 6/20 each` in the most prominent place in the tree; docs/milestones/m08.md carries the aggregate twice more in live declarative prose — `The result is a tie: arm A 6/20, arm B 6/20` at line 774, and the `A 9/20` counterfactual at 784. All are unreachable because docs/plan.md and docs/milestones/ are globally excluded. That is NOT design: whether the whole of docs/plan.md belongs on the exclude list is unsettled and filed as #367, which this file's own top `_comment` already flags. (5) THE REAL DEFENCE IS NOT THIS RAIL. It is that the figure is now DERIVED and byte-compared, so it cannot go stale at all — removing what would otherwise need enforcing, which `core/operating/evolution.md` ranks above enforcing it. This registration is the second line, and it is registered knowing the first line is the one doing the work. The option not taken: delete the aggregate outright and cite the per-cell table. It loses because the headline of a baseline is what every citing document actually needs, and a reader made to sum four rows will type the sum back into prose — recreating this defect by hand.
